payload.title: security-boundary-adapter derives route name, line, write flag, public flag and 'carries a boundary' in two separate walkers and defines a local boundary three ways (hasLocalGuardBoundary, carriesBoundary and SECURITY_DECORATORS), so a route carrying only RequiresCapability is a boundary for the peer rules and the observation but not for controller_missing_guard_boundary.

payload.rule_violated: Single owner of one fact (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 2): route decorators are read once and one predicate says what a boundary is.
payload.notes: A route with only @RequiresCapability('ops-a') in a service whose app.module registers no APP_GUARD: the endpoint observation lists RequiresCapability among its securityDecorators and the peer rule treats the route as carrying a boundary, yet hasLocalGuardBoundary is false and controller_missing_guard_boundary reports 'no guard boundary' on it. All services register an APP_GUARD and the walkers agree on the routes of apps today (review probe), so the divergence is latent; any new route decorator or public marker must be edited in two walkers. Close condition: Have analyzeEndpoints consume collectPeerClass (one reader returning name, line, writes, isPublic and one boundary predicate built from AUTHZ_DECORATORS plus UseGuards), delete the literal list at lines 237-240, decide once whether RequiresCapability is a local boundary for rules 2 and 3, and pin that the endpoint observation and the peer rows agree on a RequiresCapability-only route. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 4). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
